Minors

University Manual 8.20.50 Minor Fields of Study. Undergraduate Students may declare a “minor” field of study. A minor is a secondary concentration of courses.

18 or more credits of related studies offered by one or more departments or programs and sponsored by a faculty member. (UM 8.20.50)
At least 12 credits at the 200-level or above ( UM 8.20.51)
At least 8 credits must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.51)
Minimum GPA average of 2.0 must be earned in the minor’s required courses (UM 8.20.51)
A maximum of two courses can apply to both the major and minor field of study (UM 8.20.52)

Modality
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Identifies how a curricular offering is delivered, including in-person, online, or a combination of in-person and online instruction.
Modality
Modality identifies the method of delivery for a curricular offering, including courses, programs, and specializations. It describes whether instruction occurs in person, online, or through a combination of in-person and online instruction.
The University recognizes the following modalities:

In Person
Instruction occurs at a specified physical location on specified days and times. Less than 25% of instruction is delivered online.
In Person & Online Asynchronous
Instruction combines in-person meetings on specified days and times with online asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.
In Person & Online Synchronous
Instruction combines in-person and online meetings on specified days and times. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.

Online Synchronous
All instruction occurs online at specified days and times.
Online Synchronous & Asynchronous
All instruction occurs online and combines synchronous meetings on specified days and times with asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.
Online Asynchronous
All instruction occurs online with no required synchronous meetings at specified days and times, except for optional online office hours or meetings. The weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus.

Level
Tags: programs,specializations
Short Description: The academic level of a curricular offering (undergraduate / graduate / dual)
Level
Level identifies the academic level of a curricular offering.

Undergraduate: Courses numbered 499 and below.
Graduate — Courses numbered 500 and above.

Undergraduate: A program leading to an undergraduate degree or credential, such as a bachelor’s degree, undergraduate certificate, or minor.
Graduate: A program designed for students who have completed a bachelor’s degree and are pursuing graduate or post-baccalaureate study, including master’s degrees, doctoral degrees, graduate certificates, and other post-baccalaureate credentials.

In addition to undergraduate and graduate, proposers may select Dual for programs that provide an accelerated pathway connecting a bachelor's and master's degree, including ABM and 4+1 specializations.
Related toolkit entry: ABM
Related toolkit entry: 4+1
ABM (Accelerated Bachelor to Master's): A pathway that allows students to double-count eligible courses toward both the bachelor's and master's degrees, reducing the time required to complete the master's degree
Kuali: ABM programs are inherited from the master's degree.
4+1: A pathway that allows students to complete both a bachelor's and master's degree in five years. Unlike an ABM, a 4+1 does not include double-counted courses.
Kuali: 4+1s are inherited from the bachelors degree.

Grand Challenge
Tags: courses
Short Description: A General Education overlay centered on a complex contemporary issue and designed to engage students through interdisciplinary perspectives and ethical inquiry.
Grand Challenge
A Grand Challenge course centers on a complex issue of contemporary significance and provides students with opportunities to explore, question, and critically engage with the issue. The course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and helps students make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences. It also addresses the ethical challenges associated with the issue, providing students with opportunities to apply ethical concepts or frameworks in evaluating potential actions and their ramifications.
Proposers will complete the Grand Challenge section in their Kuali Course Proposal. This Grand Challenge Template is available as a resource to help prepare responses for submission.
